chunks: Zurarah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

That Ādam عليه السلام had a son born to him, Shīth, and that his name was Hibatullāh, and he was the first successor to whom testamentary authority was entrusted among humankind on the earth. Then after Shīth, Yāfith was born to him.

When the two reached maturity, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended to bring forth through progeny what you see, and that there be established what the Pen had already decreed regarding the prohibition of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had forbidden of sisters for brothers. So, after al-ʿAṣr on a Thursday, He sent down a heavenly maiden from Paradise whose name was Nazlah, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Ādam to marry her to Shīth, so he married her to him. Then, after al-ʿAṣr on the following day, He sent down a heavenly maiden from Paradise whose name was Munzalah, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Ādam to marry her to Yāfith, so he married her to him.

Then a boy was born to Shīth, and a girl was born to Yāfith. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Ādam, when they reached maturity, to marry the daughter of Yāfith to the son of Shīth, and he did so. Then the chosen ones from among the Prophets and the Messengers were born from their offspring. And far be it from Allah that this should have been as they have said regarding the matter of brothers and sisters.

key_terms.الصَّفْوَةُ: the chosen ones, here referring to the select Prophets and Messengers
key_terms.شِيثٌ: Sheeth, the son of Ādam عليه السلام mentioned as the first wasi among humankind
key_terms.هِبَةُ اللَّهِ: Gift of Allah; the name associated with Shīth
key_terms.وَصِيٍّ: successor or designated legatee entrusted with authority

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the continuation of human lineage after Ādam عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the early continuation of human lineage through the descendants of Ādam عليه السلام, stating that Shīth was the first wasi among humankind on earth. It presents that Allah عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ did not permit lineage to continue through marriages between brothers and sisters, but instead arranged marriages with heavenly women and then through their descendants.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4337 - Zurarah narrated from Abu Abdillah (as) that Adam (as) had a son named Sheeth, whose name means "Gift of Allah (swt)."
He was the first successor appointed among humans on earth. After Sheeth, Adam (as) had another son named Yafith.

When both sons reached maturity, Allah (swt), the Almighty and Glorious, intended to continue human progeny and fulfill what was decreed by His (swt) command. To enforce the prohibition of marriage between brothers and sisters, Allah (swt) sent down, after the afternoon (Asr) on a Thursday, a heavenly woman from Paradise named Nazlah. Allah (swt) commanded Adam (as) to marry her to Sheeth, and so he did.
The next afternoon, on Friday, Allah (swt) sent down another heavenly woman from Paradise named Munzalah.

Allah (swt) commanded Adam (as) to marry her to Yafith, and so he did.
Sheeth and Nazlah had a son, and Yafith and Munzalah had a daughter. When these children grew up, Allah (swt) commanded Adam (as) to marry the daughter of Yafith to the son of Sheeth. Adam obeyed this command, and from their lineage came the chosen ones among the prophets and messengers.
Far be it from Allah (swt) that human propagation occurred as some have claimed-through marriage between brothers and sisters. Instead, Allah (swt) ensured the preservation of purity and honor in the lineage through divine arrangements.
